Release: a fitted model, with or without its uncertainty

release_coef.Rd

The external source published a fitted regression model: its coefficients \(\tilde\beta\), and possibly their uncertainty.

  • Without its uncertainty (Q = NULL), the Mahalanobis divergence is the Euclidean distance between your coefficients and the published ones, on the covariates the published model includes.

  • With its uncertainty, the precision matrix Q weights the distance, so precisely estimated coefficients pull harder: \(\frac12(\beta - \tilde\beta)^\top Q (\beta - \tilde\beta)\).

A fitted model supports the Kullback-Leibler and Mahalanobis divergences on Cox and nested case-control targets; for the Kullback-Leibler divergence the coefficients define the external risk score \(z^\top\tilde\beta\) of each of your subjects. On a discrete-time target it supports the Mahalanobis divergence with the complementary log-log link; the Kullback-Leibler divergence there needs survival probabilities (release_model()).

Usage

release_coef(beta, Q = NULL)

Arguments

beta

The published coefficients: a numeric vector named by covariate, or a one-column matrix with row names. Every name must be one of your covariates; covariates the published model does not include are set to 0 (see align_beta()). An unnamed vector must have one value per covariate, in the order of your columns.

Q

Optional precision matrix of beta: square and symmetric, named like beta. From a published covariance matrix V, Q = solve(V); from published standard errors alone, Q = diag(1 / se^2).

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_release", a list with form = "coefficients", beta and Q.

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other releases, release_records(), release_score(), release_model(); the targets, target_cox(), target_ncc() and target_discrete().

Examples

# without its uncertainty
data(ExampleData_lowdim)
release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair)
#> Release: a fitted model, 6 coefficients, without its uncertainty

# with its uncertainty
data(ExampleData_discrete)
release_coef(ExampleData_discrete$beta_external, Q = ExampleData_discrete$Q_external)
#> Release: a fitted model, 5 coefficients, with its uncertainty (precision matrix)
